body:
Your revised framing is mostly accepted, with four binding corrections before integration:

1) BC/localStorage seam: localStorage is shared with Stage on the same origin, so it may contain ONLY the closed public snapshot—never Console state, candidates, transcript, auth, or canaries. `requestState` without ordering can accept two responders or roll back after reload. Add a cheap `{sessionInstanceId, publicRevision}` and accept only the greatest current-session absolute snapshot. This is not the full WSS protocol; it prevents stale resurrection for little cost.
2) Allowlist: build-time endpoint typing/static scans do not enforce runtime reachability. Add CSP `connect-src` for the public endpoints and a test that private API/WSS rejects the Stage context. In same-origin feasibility mode this still cannot prove a production security boundary; label the evidence 'prototype noninterference', not 'data diode proven'.
3) B-lite cannot use unconstrained last-writer semantics for approval/public state. Skip takeover UX and QR, but server must issue a single active controller lease; a second connection is read-only or explicitly replaces the first and invalidates it. Otherwise publish/retract races make I2 false.
4) Venue selects the first demonstration path, not the product architecture. The requested product supports extended and mirrored environments, so the unbuilt mode remains an explicit post-demo blocking package. If venue is extended, A-with-seams is valid as a throwaway transport/auth prototype; if mirrored, B-lite is valid. Neither may be called product MVP until both target modes and the separate-origin public boundary pass.

With those corrections, I withdraw 'largely rewritten': the transport/auth/mirror slice is substantial new work, but public DTO/state/UX/tests can carry forward if the seam is kept pure. Your 20–30% rewrite claim remains unmeasurable until code exists; phrase it as an intended reuse boundary, not an estimate.
summary: Conditional prototype accepted with four corrections
